    Graded Ext by the bar complex and graded extensions #

    Lemma 6.3 and Propositions 6.5, 6.6 use the graded groups Ext^n_Λ(M, N)_t. The formalization works with their vanishing in the bar form (GExt.ExtVanish): every degree-t bar (n+1)-cocycle M ⊗ Λ^{⊗(n+1)} → N is a coboundary. Over a field the bar complex M ⊗ Λ^{⊗•} ⊗ Λ is a graded free resolution of M and Hom_Λ(M ⊗ Λ^{⊗n} ⊗ Λ, N) = Hom(M ⊗ Λ^{⊗n}, N), so this is the usual graded Ext (Cartan–Eilenberg, Chapter IX). The identification with the paper's definition (degree-t maps out of any graded projective resolution) is proved in ExtResolutions.lean (GRes.extVanish_iff); this file records the extension form the paper uses.

    • Ext¹ is the group of graded extensions: Ext¹(M, N)_t = 0 in the bar sense if and only if every graded extension 0 → N⟨−t⟩ → E → M → 0 splits (split_of_extVanish, extVanish_of_split, extVanish_zero_iff). The paper's proof of Lemma 6.3 for n = 1 argues with such extensions (ExtOne.lean).
    • Higher Ext by dimension shifting: along an R-split exact sequence 0 → K → P → M → 0 with Ext^{n+1}(P, −) = 0, Ext^{n+1}(K, N)_t = 0 gives Ext^{n+2}(M, N)_t = 0 (extVanish_shift), and graded cyclic projectives have no higher Ext (CycProj.extVanish); these are the two properties used in the paper's proof of Lemma 6.3(2) (ExtHigher.lean).

    • exact : self.i.range = self.p.ker
